newsitem.title: CYPRUS: UN protests over Cyprus checkpoint demonstrations.
newsitem.headline: UN protests over Cyprus checkpoint demonstrations.

text.p: United Nations officials in Cyprus have complained about Greek Cypriot demonstrators attempts to discourage tourists from visiting the Turkish-occupied part of the island, a Cypriot official said on Tuesday.

Cyprus's government spokesman Yiannakis Cassoulides told reporters the U.N. intervention was made because tourists were being obstructed from visiting the Turkish-held north, with threats of retaliation from the Turkish Cypriot side.
"The government does not encourage events in the manner they are being held now and it haS clarified this from the first day," Cassoulides said.
The UN intervention came after the third consecutive weekend of protests at the U.N.-controlled Ledra Palace checkpoint, the only legal crossing from one side of the island to the other.
On Monday, a leading official in the Turkish Cypriot breakaway state said counter action would be taken if the blockades of the checkpoint continued this week.

"The Greek Cypriots' protests at the Ledra Palace checkpoint have begun to go too far," Dervis Eroglu, prime minister of the breakaway republic, recognised only by Ankara, said after a weekly meeting with Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash.
He said if the protest continues, efforts would be made to ban people crossing from the north to the south of the island.
Cyprus has been divided since a 1974 Turkish invasion after a short-lived coup in the capital Nicosia engineered by the Greek military regime at the time.
Diplomats have warned that the checkpoint protests might have a backlash on Greek Cypriots still living in the north.

"Unficyp is trying to defuse tension and would not like to see ugly reciprocal moves from the Turkish Cypriot authorities," one diplomat, referring to the peacekeeping force on the island, told Reuters.
Demonstration organisers say money being spent by tourists in the north ends up in Turkish Cypriot coffers to spend on weapons which could ultimately be used against Greek Cypriots.
